prompt: Why is `take 3` the wrong way to find the first three failures of the incident?

choices.text: It returns the last three rows instead
choices.why: It promises no order at all, first or last.

choices.text: It returns any three
choices.why: Right. `top 3 by TimeGenerated asc` sorts first.

choices.text: It cannot be combined with where
choices.why: The first query in this lesson combines them.

choices.text: It only works on tables with fewer than a thousand rows
choices.why: It works on any table, which is why it is used to peek.

prompt: The emulator answers `General_BadRequest` to your query. What is the lesson's first move?
hint: The emulator does not say which name is wrong.

choices.text: Restart the emulator, since the error is generic
choices.why: A restart loses the tables and fixes no query.

choices.text: Reload requests.kql in case the table is damaged
choices.why: The table is fine; the query names something it does not have.

choices.text: Check the names against `getschema`
choices.why: Right. A misspelt column is the commonest cause, and getschema lists the real ones.

choices.text: Switch every == to =~
choices.why: That changes case-sensitivity of comparisons, not names.

prompt: A colleague filters `where TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-10-15 14:00) .. 1h)` to see the incident, which started at 14:05 São Paulo time. What do they get?
hint: In which time zone is TimeGenerated?

choices.text: The incident, because the emulator converts to local time
choices.why: Nothing converts the filter; timestamps are UTC.

choices.text: An hour three hours before it
choices.why: Right. 14:00 UTC is 11:00 in São Paulo; convert for the reader, not for the filter.

choices.text: An error, because between needs two datetimes
choices.why: A duration as the end is allowed.

choices.text: The incident shifted by three minutes
choices.why: The offset is three hours.

prompt: Why does `thursday.kql` write `100.0 * failed / requests` and not `100 * failed / requests`?
hint: What type do two counts divide into?

choices.text: 100.0 is rounded to two places
choices.why: Rounding is done by round(); the decimal point changes the type.

choices.text: KQL refuses integer multiplication
choices.why: It multiplies integers happily.

choices.text: So the division is real, not integer
choices.why: Right. With integers, 109 * 100 / 4193 truncates.

choices.text: To express the answer as a fraction of one
choices.why: Multiplying by 100 expresses it as a percentage.

prompt: On Thursday, what percentage of checkout requests failed?
All four routes have p95 of 150 ms. What does the p99 column add?

choices.text: Nothing: p95 already describes the slow requests
choices.why: Three routes hide a near-second tail beyond the 95th percentile.

choices.text: That a slow tail sits past it in three routes
choices.why: Right. The tail shows only past the 95th percentile here.

choices.text: That checkout's average is wrong
choices.why: The average is computed correctly; it just hides the tail.

choices.text: That the incident is included in GET /products
choices.why: The incident touched checkout only.

prompt: In `window.kql`, the 17:00 bin shows 9 failures out of 37. Why not the full two in three?
hint: When did the incident start inside that bin?

choices.text: The emulator samples rows inside a bin
choices.why: Every row is counted.

choices.text: Failures are counted at the end of the bin
choices.why: Rows are counted where they fall, all through the bin.

choices.text: The incident began at 17:05, halfway through
choices.why: Right. The bin mixes five normal minutes with five failing ones.

choices.text: Ten-minute bins average the failure rate
choices.why: countif counts; it does not average.

prompt: A service starts answering 500 in 20 ms instead of failing slowly. Which of window.kql's columns moves, and which way?
hint: A fast error is still an error.

choices.text: Both rise together, as on Thursday
choices.why: They rose together because Thursday's failures were timeouts.

choices.text: failed rises; p95 stays low
choices.why: Right. Fast errors pull latency down, which is why both signals are watched.

choices.text: p95 rises; failed stays flat
choices.why: A 500 is a failure whatever its speed.

choices.text: Neither, because 20 ms is under the bin size
choices.why: Bin size is about time grouping, not request duration.

prompt: Unlike summarize by bin(), the operator ___ fills empty time slots with a default value instead of leaving them out.
hint: Lesson 25 uses it; it has a hyphen.

choices.text: KQL refuses a join without a kind
choices.why: It accepts one and uses its own default.

choices.text: leftouter is faster than every other kind of join in KQL
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: So a route with no owner stays in the answer
choices.why: Right. And the default kind is not the inner join people expect, so naming it avoids a surprise.

choices.text: To join on two columns instead of one
choices.why: The columns are named by `on`, not by kind.

prompt: The weekly report shows catalogue with 135 failures and payments with 130. What does this lesson conclude?
hint: How were the failures spread in time?

choices.text: Catalogue had the worse week
choices.why: Its failures were spread thin over seven days.

choices.text: The two teams had an equally bad week
choices.why: Similar totals, very different experiences for customers.

choices.text: Payments had the incident, hidden by the total
choices.why: Right. Almost all of payments' failures fell in 42 minutes; a total answers how many, not how bad.

choices.text: The join double-counted payments
choices.why: Each route appears once on the right; nothing doubled.

prompt: Put the lines of owners.kql's main query in the order they run.
trap: Joining before summarizing is the slip: it works, and attaches a team to a quarter of a million rows instead of four.

prompt: How many slow failed checkouts did the `local` query count in Thursday's incident?
Which of these does KQL do in this lesson exactly as a Log Analytics workspace would? Choose all that apply.
hint: The language is the same; the editor and the charts are not.

choices.text: Computing a 99th percentile with percentile()
choices.why: Yes. Same engine, same function.

choices.text: Grouping by bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
choices.why: Yes. Identical.

choices.text: Naming the misspelt column in an error
choices.why: No. The emulator answers General_BadRequest; a workspace names the column.

choices.text: Drawing render timechart as a chart
choices.why: No. The emulator returns tables; a workspace draws them.
